matches.gold_text: Proposals must be received by the City by 3:00 p.m. PT on September 17, 2024.
Proposals must not be submitted by fax.
The vendor must offer ERP software and services that satisfy all of the City's functional and technical requirements.
The preferred vendor has experience successfully implementing the proposed solutions for cities of similar size and scope of services.
Any best-of-breed Human Capital Management solution offered must be able to integrate with the selected ERP system.
A vendor responding with a best-of-breed solution must complete the Section 6 Requirements template for the relevant functionality and submit it per the Section 5 instructions.
The vendor must provide an integrated ERP solution that includes the modules and functionality defined in the Requirements document.
The replacement ERP solution is to be implemented in phases or as recommended by the selected vendor and approved by the City.
Vendors invited to demonstrate their product should be prepared to discuss the application's best practices and its ability to adapt to user preferences.
The City's estimated implementation window runs from March 2025 through January 2027.
All modules in scope must go live by January 1, 2027.
Finalist vendors must follow the City's pre-defined script during their software demonstrations.
The proposal must be one electronic PDF copy, in the order defined in the response format table, not exceeding 100 total pages excluding sample contracts.
matches.reason: 100-page limit excluding sample contract matches; PDF format and order not stated, but core limit matches.

matches.gold_text: The response must include one completed copy of the Requirements document in MS Word format, with the Word format unmodified.
Proposals should be emailed to the City contact at Thuch.Mam@FederalWayWA.gov.
All data, materials and documentation originated and prepared for the City under this solicitation belong to the City.
Vendor questions about the RFP may be submitted by email to the City contact by August 28, 2024, 3:00 p.m. PT.
matches.reason: Candidates omit the August 28, 2024 3:00 p.m. PT question deadline.

matches.gold_text: Vendor responses should include the sections outlined in the Proposal Response Format; deviation may lead to the response being deemed non-responsive and disqualified.
Marketing literature should not be included in the proposal.
The proposal must begin with a cover letter that is an executive summary of the proposed software and services, limited to two pages.
The vendor must complete the Pricing Summary from Exhibit A, indicating costs for software and implementation services.
Pricing must be comprehensive, including all taxes and available discounts.
Pricing must remain valid for 180 days from the response date.
The vendor must price the software for the user counts defined in the RFP.
The vendor must provide a separate pricing sheet for each deployment option offered (SaaS or on-premises).
matches.reason: One pricing sheet per deployment option, SaaS or on-premises.

matches.gold_text: Implementation pricing must include all costs required for go-live, including software deployment, data conversion, system configuration, report development, testing and training.
The vendor must price ongoing license and maintenance for Years 1-10.
Financials software must be priced for 130 named users and 85 concurrent users.
Human Capital Management software must be priced for 400 FTEs and 744 W2s.

The proposal must include an implementation overview covering methodology, sample project plan, City and vendor resources, process improvement, change management, data conversion, testing, training and report development.
The proposal must include an overview of support services offered, including hours, response times, support tiers, post go-live services, backup and disaster recovery.
The proposal must include a technology overview covering architecture and deployment options, data centers, hardware, mobile, remote access, integration tools and software updates.
The proposal must include a security overview covering the security model, standards, SSO/SAML administration, multi-factor authentication and breach response.
The vendor must provide references from three current and two prior customers for the proposed software, using the Exhibit B forms.
Preference is for references from Washington State public sector clients.
The vendor must disclose any contract terminations or legal actions with customers in the past five years, describing each situation with the contracting party's name and address.
The proposal must include sample contract documents such as a statement of work, license agreement, maintenance or support agreements and service level agreements.
The vendor must document any exceptions it has to the RFP content.
The vendor's Requirements responses will be incorporated into the signed contract.
matches.reason: No candidate says requirements responses are incorporated into the contract.

matches.gold_text: The vendor must provide a rating and a comment for every item in the Requirements document; blank responses may cause rejection.
matches.reason: Rating and comment required for each requirement.

matches.gold_text: The vendor must not include hyperlinks in the Requirements document.
The vendor must not modify the format, font or numbering of the Requirements section or insert page breaks.
Requirement comments must give a substantive explanation; generic comments such as "Standard Functionality" are unacceptable.
Each line-item response in the Requirements document must be limited to 100 words.
The vendor must provide a certification of insurance before commencing any work.
An underwriter's endorsement with additional insured verbiage is required, and the surety must be admitted in the State of Washington.

matches.reason: No candidate mentions replacing the Excel budget process.

matches.reason: No candidate mentions replacing Excel ACFR preparation.

consistency.reason: Largely respects the constraints, but the 100-word, per-cell requirement response rules and the 100-page limit go unaddressed. The plan also leaves no month for hypercare after January 1 go-live.

component_records.title: Programme mobilisation and phased implementation plan
component_records.description: Establishes the delivery structure the City approves before configuration starts: a four-phase plan (mobilise and fit-gap, configure and convert, test and train, cutover and post-go-live) with phase gates, a sample project plan of phases, tasks and dates, and a resourcing model naming City roles and Vendor roles with responsibilities and average hours per month. The plan is built backwards from the January 1, 2027 go-live for all modules and sits inside the March 2025 to January 2027 implementation window, with the final month reserved for hypercare rather than new scope. It sets out the defined and proven implementation methodology the Vendor applies, including how fit-gap decisions, change control and phase sign-off work, and it carries the process improvement strategy that moves City processes onto the product's standard practices with named process owners accepting each change. Business change management methodology and tools are part of the same plan, covering stakeholder mapping, readiness assessments and communications per phase.

component_records.title: Financials module configuration
component_records.description: Configures and implements the Financials scope: General Ledger, Budget, Project and Grant Accounting, Purchasing and Contract Management, Accounts Payable, Accounts Receivable, Capital Assets and Enterprise Cashiering. Each module is configured against the City's item-by-item responses in the Requirements document, with every item rated 4, 3, 2, 0 or F and a comment on how the function is met, so the delivered configuration can be traced back to the City's own requirement list. Items rated 2 are delivered as modifications with an estimated cost stated against each, and items rated 3 name the third-party application that supplies the function. The component also covers the functional depth the City scores under its Software criterion, including the budget-to-actual, grant accounting and cashiering processes the City names in scope.

component_records.title: Human Capital Management configuration and best-of-breed integration
component_records.description: Configures Human Resources, Time and Attendance and Payroll for the City's 400 FTEs and 744 W2s, including position control, time capture rules, payroll calendars and deduction and accrual setup. Where the City selects a best-of-breed HCM product instead of the ERP vendor's own HCM module, this component delivers the integration between that product and the selected ERP system, using published APIs and file-based interfaces for employee master data, time entries and payroll postings, and demonstrates that integration in the product demo. The integration architecture, tools and methodology are documented so the City can see how the two systems stay in step after go-live.

component_records.title: Data conversion and report development
component_records.description: Runs the data conversion methodology: source-to-target mapping per module, extraction from the City's existing ERP, cleansing, mock conversions and reconciliation sign-off by City process owners before each cutover. The conversion plan is recommended module by module and states the years of history, the data elements converted and the treatment of open balances, open purchase orders, active employees and year-to-date payroll. Report development covers the City's operational and statutory reports, built on the product's reporting tools with a report inventory agreed in fit-gap and tested against converted data. Both workstreams are priced inside implementation services so that conversion and reporting effort is visible to the City rather than absorbed into a contingency.

component_records.title: Testing, training and change management
component_records.description: Delivers the testing methodology and tools: unit, integration, conference-room pilot, user acceptance and parallel or pilot payroll runs, with defect tracking and entry and exit criteria per cycle. Training covers role-based curricula for Financials and HCM users, train-the-trainer for City super-users, quick reference guides and a sandbox environment, sized to the City's 130 named and 85 concurrent Financials users and its HCM population. Change management runs alongside, using the business change management methodology and tools set out in the implementation plan to prepare process owners and end users for the new standard practices. Training and change effort is priced within implementation services through go live.

component_records.title: Hosted platform, technology architecture and security
component_records.description: Provides the hosted SaaS platform and, where the City prefers it, an on-premises deployment, with the technical architecture, database, data centre locations and redundancy, hardware specifications, mobile device and operating system support, and remote access arrangements documented for the City's Technology evaluation. Accessibility is addressed against the City's IT strategy, including the accessibility conformance the platform meets and how it is tested. Security covers the security model, the standards the system meets, single sign-on and SAML administration, multi-factor authentication, and breach handling with the customer communication, response and cost position stated. Software updates are described as scheduled releases with a stated cadence and a City notification window, and integration tools and methodologies are documented for both deployment models.

component_records.title: Pricing model and cost submission
component_records.description: Builds the City's Pricing Summary from Exhibit A as the single price book for the bid: software cost for 130 named and 85 concurrent Financials users and for 400 FTEs and 744 W2s of HCM, Year 1 software priced module by module for the Financials and HCM scopes, implementation services covering implementation, data conversion, training, report development, integration, travel and other, and subscription or maintenance for each of Years 2 through 10. One sheet is prepared per deployment option, so SaaS and on-premises are priced separately and the City can compare them. All figures are comprehensive of taxes and available discounts, remain valid for 180 days from the response date, and carry stated assumptions alongside each of the software, implementation and maintenance lines. The bid team's own bid and proposal costs are carried by the Vendor and not passed to the City.

component_records.title: Contract, compliance and insurance obligations
component_records.description: A contract and compliance workstream owns the non-technical obligations. It records the Vendor's acknowledgment and acceptance of all terms and conditions in the RFP and its exhibits, with any exceptions documented rather than left implicit. It confirms that ownership of all data, materials and documentation originated and prepared for the City under the solicitation rests with the City, and that the contract reflects that. It provides a certification of insurance before any work begins, evidenced by an underwriter's endorsement containing additional insured verbiage, placed with a surety admitted in the State of Washington. It also carries the Vendor's organisational strength and government entity experience position and its comparable-city implementation record, evidenced through the reference forms in Exhibit B.

component_records.title: Demo, evaluation and post-go-live support
component_records.description: Prepares the Vendor for the City's evaluation events: attendance at the City's pre-demo meetings on demo logistics and script, delivery of the functional and technical demonstration strictly to the pre-defined script, and demonstration of the product's ability to meet the City's functional and technical requirements, including best practices and the system's adaptability to user preferences. The same team stands ready to supply additional information, interviews, follow-up demonstrations and clarifications during evaluation. After go-live the component delivers post go-live tools and services, support hours, guaranteed response times, escalation, baseline versus premium support, user groups and conferences, and the backup and disaster recovery position covering backup, redundancy and location.

If any phase gate slips, the contractual go-live date is missed and the City's Implementation score (25 of 100 points) is lost. Without them the bid cannot be sized, priced or answered item by item, and the 100-word-per-item response and rating scale cannot be applied. The bid team risks pricing a scope it has guessed. The Requirements document is the basis for the Software criterion (30 points) and for the item-by-item pricing of modifications, and it is confirmed missing from the package.

items.text: Exhibit A pricing template and Exhibit B reference forms missing. Rebuilding the template risks a non-responsive price book, and the City may award on the proposal alone without discussion, so a malformed pricing sheet cannot be corrected later. The same applies to the five references that must be on the City's own forms. The documents are confirmed absent, but the City may reissue them with the addenda, so the likelihood turns on facts the RFP does not settle.

items.text: Best-of-breed HCM integration has no defined target ERP. The RFP allows a best-of-breed HCM product but requires it to integrate with the selected ERP system, which is not yet chosen. The proposed solution assumes published APIs and file-based interfaces and defers confirmation of the target ERP and interface standards to contract. If the City selects a different ERP or requires real-time interfaces rather than batch files, the integration design and its price change after award. The integration obligation is mandatory for a best-of-breed bid, and the RFP leaves the target system and standards open, so the design risk is real but depends on the City's later selection.

items.text: Questions deadline conflict risks losing clarifications. One clause sets vendor questions due August 28, 2024 at 3:00 p.m. PT while another requires all questions in writing before the Section 3 timeline date, which is the September 17, 2024 proposal deadline. If the bid team relies on the later date, questions on scope, insurance and the missing exhibits go unanswered and the bid is priced on assumptions. The two dates are three weeks apart and the earlier one is the safe reading, so a team that follows the later clause will miss the answer window.

The RFP requires a certification of insurance, an underwriter's endorsement with additional insured verbiage and a Washington-admitted surety before any work begins, but states no coverage types or limits. The proposed solution assumes limits customary for a public-sector ERP implementation. If the City's contract requires higher limits or a performance bond, the cost lands on the bidder after the price is fixed. The obligation is mandatory and pre-work, but the exposure depends on limits the RFP does not give, so the impact is a cost the bidder absorbs rather than a failed bid.
items.reason: Insurance requirements and absence of limits supported; the proposed solution's customary-limits assumption and performance bond are not in sources.

Proposal page limit and required structure are ambiguous. The proposed solution carries a large implementation, technology, security and support narrative that will not fit if the cap is hard and inclusive. items.text: Process improvement and best-practice adoption not defined or accepted. The City requires process improvement through adopting the Vendor's best practices but does not define which practices are in scope or how acceptance is evidenced. The proposed solution treats fit-gap sign-off by named City process owners as the acceptance mechanism. If City staff resist moving off current practices, fit-gap extends and the January 1, 2027 date is exposed. The requirement is mandatory and the acceptance route is an assumption in the solution, so the risk is a schedule slip rather than a scope failure.

items.text: Demo script not issued so demo preparation is unsized. Finalists must demo strictly to a pre-defined script that is issued only with the invitation, and demo performance counts in the evaluation. The proposed solution resources demo preparation on the assumption that the script and timing arrive with the invitation. If the script covers modules or scenarios the team has not rehearsed, the demo score suffers on a 100-point evaluation. The script is confirmed missing and the notification date is not given, so the preparation window is unknown; the impact is a scoring loss rather than a failed delivery.

items.text: Reference eligibility undefined for the five required customers. The RFP requires three current and two prior customers on Exhibit B forms, with preference for Washington State public sector clients, but does not define what makes a customer comparable in size or scope, or what Population means. The proposed solution assumes Washington public-sector ERP references reported by resident population. If the City applies a stricter comparability test, references may be rejected and the Vendor criterion (15 points) lost. The requirement is mandatory and the comparability test is undefined, so the outcome depends on the City's unstated threshold.

items.text: Deployment model and user-count basis drive the price. The RFP asks for one pricing sheet per deployment option if applicable but does not say whether both SaaS and on-premises must be priced, and the user counts that govern software pricing are referenced rather than restated in the pricing section. The proposed solution prices SaaS as primary and on-premises on a second sheet against 130 named and 85 concurrent Financials users and 400 FTEs and 744 W2s. If the City reads concurrency or named-user definitions differently, the licence price moves after submission. The price book is the Cost Value criterion (15 points) and the basis is unsettled, so a definitional difference changes the price without changing the scope.
items.reason: Claim that user counts are only referenced, not restated in pricing section, is contradicted: Exhibit A restates 130/85/400/744 counts.
